commit_message:
[wasm][deoptimizer] Resolve feedback vector in WasmLiftoffDeoptFinish only

Previously the deoptimizer would try to lookup the feedback vector in
the vector of feedback vectors in the wasm trusted instance.
This was implemented at a time when I still assumed that there will
always be a valid feedback vector, however due to multi-instance
scenarios, this turned out to be incorrect. Later on this was fixed in
the WasmLiftoffDeoptFinish to allocate and fill in those feedback
vectors for which we didn't find one yet.

Moving the lookup of the feedback vector to the builtin exclusively
simplifies the code and also removes an access to the heap from within
the deoptimizer (which we'd ideally reduce down to zero if possible).

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 4e101ceb0b0b on top of intro 8d161a06cdbf via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): When --trace-deopt-verbose is enabled, Runtime_WasmLiftoffDeoptFinish in src/runtime/runtime-wasm.cc logs the wasm function being deoptimized by calling NativeModule::GetCode(). It passes a 'declared function index' (relative to the module's non-imported functions) into GetCode(), which expects a 'module function index' (including imported functions) and internally re-derives the declared index by subtracting num_imported_functions. This double conversion produces an incorrect (potentially negative) index used to access the NativeModule's code_table_ array, leading to an out-of-bounds read / DCHECK failure and an incorrect diagnostic function index/name being logged. Root cause: Two different kinds of wasm function indices exist in V8's codebase: the 'declared function index' (excludes imported functions) and the 'module function index' (includes imported functions). NativeModule::GetCode() expects the latter and performs its own conversion via declared_function_index(). The introducing commit passed the already-declared index directly to GetCode() without converting it back to a module-scoped index, causing the conversion to be applied twice.
